title: Why Atoms Bond: Octet Rule Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Salt and water are made of atoms that hold on to each other, but helium atoms in a party balloon float alone. Why? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 4, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure) we open the chapter with the Kossel-Lewis approach and the octet rule.

You will see why a full outer shell (8 electrons, or 2 for helium) makes the noble gases so stable, watch sodium give its outer electron to chlorine on the molecule bench (Kossel, 1916, ionic or electrovalent bond), and watch two chlorine atoms share a pair instead (Lewis, covalent bond). We draw Lewis symbols for C, N, O, F and Ne step by step, find valence from the dots, and work out the formula and electrovalence of magnesium fluoride. Then the exam trap, an original JEE and NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 38 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:

0:30 Why eight? A full outer shell
0:56 Kossel: sodium gives, chlorine takes
1:35 Lewis: two chlorine atoms share
1:58 Pause and think: give or share?
2:11 Lewis symbols step by step
2:45 The octet rule
2:52 Worked example: MgF2
3:30 Exam trap and where it is asked
